prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants in Denver — the right provider depends on the complexity of your case and your priorities (experience with full-mouth vs single-tooth implants, sedation, price, timing, cosmetic skill, etc.). I can help you find someone, but first here are practical steps and criteria to pick the best provider for you.

Who to look for
- Specialists for implants: oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS), periodontists, and prosthodontists. General dentists with advanced implant training or fellowships can also be excellent for straightforward cases.
- Board certification and affiliations: American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, American Board of Periodontology, American Board of Prosthodontics, or membership in the American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) are good signals of additional training/commitment.

What to prioritize
- Experience and case mix: years placing implants, number of implants placed, and experience with cases like yours (bone grafting, sinus lifts, full-arch restorations).
- Technology and planning: cone-beam CT (CBCT) imaging, guided-surgery planning, digital restorations — these reduce surprises and improve outcomes.
- Team approach: coordination between the surgeon who places the implant and the dentist/prosthodontist who makes the crown/bridge is important for esthetics and function.
- Follow-up & warranty: ask about postoperative follow-up, success rates, and any guarantees or maintenance plans.
- Patient reviews & before/after photos: look for consistent positive feedback about results, pain management, and communication.

Questions to ask at a consult
- How many implants have you placed and how many similar to my case?
- Are you board certified or do you have advanced implant fellowship training?
- Will you use CBCT and computer-guided planning?
- Who will do my restoration (crown/bridge/prosthesis)? Is that person in your office or a referring dentist?
- What are the risks, expected timeline, and total cost (placement, grafts, restoration)?
- What sedation or pain control options do you offer?
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references?

Where to search for candidates
- AAID, American Academy of Periodontology, or professional board directories
- Local dental schools (University of Colorado) for experienced faculty or referrals
- Google/Healthgrades/Yelp for patient reviews, but verify credentials on state licensing board

If you want, tell me:
- Your ZIP code or neighborhood in Denver
- Whether the case is a single tooth, multiple teeth, or full-arch
- Any budget or insurance constraints
and I’ll compile a short list of highly rated local providers and what to ask each one.
